To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pore-scale diffusivity of a nanoparticle is spatially dependent and that the void space of a three-dimensional porous media is more limited than previously assumed.

1) the diffusion of particles deep inside the pores of a porous medium is significantly hindered and spatially heterogeneous, 2) the diffusion of larger particles is even more hindered than smaller particles, and 3) the accessibility of the void spaces in the pores of this medium is limited and depends on particle size.
the diffusion of nanoparticles in three-dimensional porous media is more heterogeneous than previously expected.

the study of diffusion and flow in complex porous media, such as the ones encountered in geology and in porous polymer materials.
the development of new porous materials and the understanding of their properties at the molecular and microscopic level.
the transport of nanoparticles through a three-dimensional porous structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pore-scale diffusion and void accessibility of nanoparticles in a 3D porous material are more complex than previously expected.
we have demonstrated that particle mobility is strongly size dependent and that the void space in a 3D porous material is not accessible to all particles, but is instead highly heterogeneous.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diffusion and transport of particles within a porous material is strongly dependent on the pore size distribution, the pore shape and the particle size distribution.
the pore-scale heterogeneity in a three-dimensional material can be quantified using a single-particle tracking technique.
we have demonstrated that single particle tracking can be used to study diffusion and accessibility of porous materials, and that the pore scale heterogeneity of diffusion is significant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diffusion of particles in porous media is more complicated than previously thought.
nanoparticle motion in a porous material is not simply a function of particle size.
